messages:
theo: FYI seeing repeated SLO blips (1-2s tails) for small-chat tenants in eu-west-1 during nightly GC/checkpoint window. Appears correlated with PCIe write bursts from a handful of pods.
rachel: are these on MIG or full-GPU hosts?
theo: mixed. some are 1g. others are full GPU. telemetry shows GPU PCIe_bw_util spiking near 90% and NIC egress jitter rising.
samir: that smells like checkpointing hitting local NVMe then DMA to GPU memory causing bus contention. Have we ruled out noisy host firmware retries?
theo: kernel logs show some retries but nothing fatal. pattern: 02:00-02:30 UTC nightly flush from 3 tenants, repeated for 4 nights.
infra-bot: ALERT: pcie_bandwidth_util > 80% on rack r-eu-07 for 15m (auto-annotated).
jules: quick mitigations:
- schedule tenant checkpoint staggering using Optimize suggestions (shift dev heavy checkpoints into off-peak windows)
- temporary dedicated carveout: mark those tenants as `dedicated=carveout-ephemeral` so scheduler reserves isolated hosts
- enforce pod annotation `redwood.io/blkio-bps: "write=50MB"` via admission controller to cap write bursts
- if still noisy, migrate to dedicated-pool (reserved) and enable pre-warm KV cache
samir: +1 for admission controller enforcement. Manual sysfs tweaks are brittle. Also add a node-level egress shaping rule to avoid NIC queues building up.
rachel: cost tradeoff: moving to dedicated reserved pool increases monthly committed spend but reduces SLO incidents. Need quick calc: which tenants have >1k qps or >2TB/wk checkpoint volume?
theo: I pulled a report: three tenants fit that bill; one is non-production but heavy. Suggest we ask them to opt into preemptible-backed dedicated slices for the canary.
infra-bot: NOTE: scheduled migration job 3780011222-migrate-heavy-checkpoints at 2024-10-05T02:10:00Z (queued).
jules: operational plan for tonight's canary:
1) label affected pods `redwood.experimental.dedicated: "true"` (kube patch snippet below)
```
kubectl -n tenant-foo patch pod foo-checkpoint -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"redwood.experimental.dedicated":"true"}}}'
```
2) admission controller applies `blkio` annotation and runtime sidecar enforces throttling
3) observe pcie_bandwidth_util, gpu_kv_miss_rate, and tail_latency for 30m
4) if tails persist, trigger `migrate-to-dedicated-pool` runbook (auto-assign to reserved hosts)
samir: add rollback: remove label, scale-down reserved hosts, and revert admission controller policy. Also collect pcap on one affected node for NIC diagnostics.
rachel: can we instead route heavy checkpoint writes to S3 with chunked, rate-limited uploader in the runtime? That avoids local NVMe noise but costs egress and S3 PUTs. Measure delta for canary.
jules: yep include cost delta capture step. Also add an Optimize rule: if checkpoint_size > 1GB, recommend chunked+quiet-upload.
theo: timeline: canary at 02:10 UTC, two nodes, 4 pods. I'll trigger and post logs here.
infra-bot: INFO: canary started 3780011222-canary-carveout at 2024-10-05T02:10:12Z.
samir: one more ask: add routing fallback so that if a node's pcie util >85% and latency >1s we route new allocations to eu-west-2 instead of forcing cross-region egress. That preserves latency for existing local customers.
rachel: agreed. update routing policy `region-prefer` rules and add a temporary hard-avoid for r-eu-07.
theo: I'll update policy and push canary. will post results in ~45m.
jules: no objections. prefer admission-controlled throttle + routing shift first, then migrate to paid dedicated if needed.
infra-bot: RESULT: canary step 1/4 completed. telemetry: pcie_util down 30%, tail_latency reduced ~40% on affected tenants. Detailed metrics: https://metrics.redwood.internal/3780011222/canary
theo: excellent. will open a short RFC to propose a recurring scheduler window and Optimize checkpoint rules. closing for now.
